paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's word stands even when the messenger gets punished for saying it. Jeremiah said what the LORD told him, and Pashhur, the chief official in the house of the LORD, answered with a beating and the stocks (Jeremiah 20:1-2). But locking up the messenger doesn't lock up the message. The next day Jeremiah walked out and said it again, and he said more (Jeremiah 20:3-4).

Now look at what Pashhur had been doing. He'd been prophesying lies to his friends, and the LORD says so right to his face (Jeremiah 20:6). I think that's a hard thing to hear when you're the one with the keys and the title. Being in charge near holy things doesn't make you right, and the LORD doesn't grade on position. He looks at whether you're listening to Him.

So what does this mean for you, baker? Sometimes the true word is the unwelcome word, and a comfortable voice isn't always a faithful one. When you read Scripture, let it tell you what it says, even when you were hoping for something softer. And if you ever stand for what's true and it costs you, remember that Jeremiah got out of those stocks and kept right on speaking.
